"""omp — Bazel build for the native (Rust) side of the workspace.

Builds the pi_natives NAPI cdylib for every shipped target with hermetic
toolchains, replacing cargo-zigbuild/cargo-xwin/sccache plus the hand-rolled
CI caches with Bazel's content-addressed action cache (see infra/docs/03-caching.md).

Layout:
  //:natives-<target>      release-grade renamed .node artifacts (root BUILD.bazel)
  //crates/...             first-party crate targets
  //bazel/...              platforms, ISA-variant constraints, toolchains, rules
  @crates//...             third-party crates from Cargo.lock via crate_universe

The cargo workspace stays authoritative for local iteration (rust-analyzer,
`cargo nextest`, napi typedef regeneration); Bazel is the artifact and CI
pipeline. `crate_universe` derives @crates from Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock; its result is cached in
MODULE.bazel.lock, which must be refreshed with them: `bun run gen:bazel-lock`.
"""

module(name = "omp")

bazel_dep(name = "bazel_skylib", version = "1.8.2")
bazel_dep(name = "platforms", version = "1.1.0")
bazel_dep(name = "rules_rust", version = "0.71.3")
bazel_dep(name = "hermetic_cc_toolchain", version = "4.2.0")

# zig-wrapper patches (rationale in each patch header):
# - zig 0.14's cache corrupts under concurrent `zig cc` (ziglang/zig#18763);
#   compile-only steps get private throwaway caches, links keep the shared one.
# - rustc's -Wl,--fix-cortex-a53-843419 on aarch64 linux links is dropped;
#   zig cc rejects it as an unsupported linker arg.
# - standalone compiler --version probes bypass Zig-only target syntax;
#   code keeps glibc 2.17, and rustc's deprecated no-op -Wl,-O1 is omitted.
single_version_override(
    module_name = "hermetic_cc_toolchain",
    patch_strip = 1,
    patches = [
        "//bazel/patches:hermetic_cc_toolchain-isolated-compile-cache.patch",
        "//bazel/patches:hermetic_cc_toolchain-drop-cortex-a53-link-arg.patch",
        "//bazel/patches:hermetic_cc_toolchain-authoritative-target.patch",
    ],
)

# rules_rust 0.71.3 writes `DEP_<links>_*` paths into a build script's out_dir
# with an `${out_dir}` token that dependents' build scripts never resolve, so
# e.g. tree-sitter's `DEP_WASMTIME_C_API_INCLUDE` pointed nowhere. The patch
# keeps those paths exec-root relative (`${pwd}/bazel-out/.../_bs.out_dir/...`);
# dependents already receive the out_dir as an input.
single_version_override(
    module_name = "rules_rust",
    patch_strip = 1,
    patches = ["//bazel/patches:rules_rust-dep-env-exec-root-paths.patch"],
)

# --- Rust toolchains ----------------------------------------------------------
rust = use_extension("@rules_rust//rust:extensions.bzl", "rust")
rust.toolchain(
    edition = "2024",
    extra_target_triples = [
        "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu",
        "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu",
        "x86_64-unknown-linux-musl",
        "aarch64-unknown-linux-musl",
        "x86_64-apple-darwin",
        "aarch64-apple-darwin",
        "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc",
        "aarch64-pc-windows-msvc",
    ],
    # Pinned archive checksums for every toolchain component. Not (only) a
    # supply-chain nicety: rules_rust marks a toolchain-tools repo as
    # reproducible — and therefore eligible for Bazel's repo contents cache —
    # only when every sha256 it needs was predeclared here (repositories.bzl:
    # `reproducible = sha256s == dict(ctx.attr.sha256s)`). Without these,
    # every fresh output base (= every ephemeral CI pod) re-downloaded and
    # re-extracted ~5 rustc toolchains (~20 s each). Regenerate after a
    # version bump: for each `<tool>-nightly-<triple>` below, take the value
    # from https://static.rust-lang.org/dist/<date>/<file>.tar.xz.sha256.
    sha256s = {
        "2026-11-08/cargo-nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.xz": "a6830e8340f7076be4f07412a4e40aa210c4226f13a89a3ebe4dc724f101f1fc",
        "2026-11-08/cargo-nightly-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz": "c419030d0b5fefcfc6a587633c975d0c13bbe27a69051a5057aa601fa97fce25",
        "2026-11-08/cargo-nightly-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.xz": "9abf042effbd4877c8e706ed16ece07926edae75510b9f4128f992e87308bba9",
        "2026-11-08/cargo-nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz": "933f57c1ca9ab478f29b04ed536a3c12ec500124165b2865b4de551aaa35e8a2",
        "2026-11-08/clippy-nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.xz": "21a27c0db5589324ee7a8d123fc628d412f000a81548fb9f74ff7f43656d7886",
        "2026-11-08/clippy-nightly-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz": "fdaebed71e8f9a78486c80ef72216571d01317044b515814ddc8f1be52ecca4d",
        "2026-11-08/clippy-nightly-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.xz": "4af645bb989689427b99f6c01d7c171bf46c160d98b02d18489913e487a0995f",
        "2026-11-08/clippy-nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz": "380a5f277e882e9cc095a85183f924babce167b54ad8b87f52726ce92a3bea2c",
        "2026-11-08/llvm-tools-nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.xz": "82deac4f030550078a346d0c08e87e66130cde150275ac9548afbf0195febaa8",
        "2026-11-08/llvm-tools-nightly-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz": "1af51afec11bece5554bc60941b1d7dcbc9581ad27e5c4abf3e2dc850f95106c",
        "2026-11-08/llvm-tools-nightly-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.xz": "28e47e4a116aad9c09ffe30322e33971a53fc74cbea566030baeb5d2eeaa200c",
        "2026-11-08/llvm-tools-nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz": "18f2eb0b8f48c85eb9104996f43d25ca9d632581fb9fae9d70f1d806091621ce",
        "2026-11-08/rust-src-nightly.tar.xz": "141d8e767382cd839feff84c7cf6937656c53de8997a313c3bbf56b03cae3c45",
        "2026-11-08/rust-std-nightly-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.tar.xz": "76c1a9ab1e9efbbb77bd179f1fe365952daecfbc1796bbb19ee90754221bfcfb",
        "2026-11-08/rust-std-nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.xz": "b281bdc8c8d0217d3d8aafbe77f763246014fd925068f41c20a6efed57e62b8c",
        "2026-11-08/rust-std-nightly-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz": "dccff165f3cbb7fe622c11c6efdb9b18a37d38eaf2663d8c402e321f301dc178",
        "2026-11-08/rust-std-nightly-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.xz": "3af90e6db4580f3b9d526cf5ee76d9cd231dc26984c9227678bbdbd8ffd2de19",
        "2026-11-08/rust-std-nightly-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.xz": "6b459120e0d47e01729bb91c63492c07e70ef6f6fe081721a09d8c4886e5f16c",
        "2026-11-08/rust-std-nightly-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.tar.xz": "d1d26602d89f981f07e0607be5b4f35764e0f8b2413801c294f4b682b335d314",
        "2026-11-08/rust-std-nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz": "db82d4ea1684d490eb3a49666676e9a8793d271dfeb8c2998342f4b41d16c46d",
        "2026-11-08/rust-std-nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.xz": "a603626f29e4e338c2a7ed4ecc7f5ee04271274d7f5f78a87ce6bc64367001bb",
        "2026-11-08/rustc-nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.xz": "c47e0efb800c2f19ead41dc57b4c09f3a708d9d260a7e498ef10124415cd8150",
        "2026-11-08/rustc-nightly-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz": "9d9017dced5afaf38cbcb1ee875372b9e3fa527f56879b700542b2e08ada15e8",
        "2026-11-08/rustc-nightly-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.xz": "e4a52857f7e205e17f91a1d13e0ee9132c23b2c9e0950f91fbe71cb4886f55fe",
        "2026-11-08/rustc-nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz": "9c7cf72535dd83b68e920ff9235466dd613d844f531f41b6478175491315d4a7",
        "2026-11-08/rustfmt-nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.xz": "c1007e511d6c2910bd81ad0bf3fd7da5fdd1eb751f15ebaf65078c0068f09012",
        "2026-11-08/rustfmt-nightly-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz": "eba54ca81357c3b75589a71a814e70909de22ec38628b4dc94912c9c32be9c41",
        "2026-11-08/rustfmt-nightly-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.xz": "a583905d6499432c53f58ab42ce057539cb43a8f2abf326a6841dd4b070c972e",
        "2026-11-08/rustfmt-nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz": "b3bd6de853e05c30a3803e2e3b06660a3d20e2195cd419ddc7df3ef70ee99b16",
    },
    # rules_rust otherwise fetches rustfmt at its own DEFAULT_NIGHTLY_VERSION,
    # which drifts from the toolchain (and from `cargo fmt`) on every bump.
    rustfmt_version = "nightly/2026-11-08",
    versions = ["nightly/2026-11-08"],
)
use_repo(
    rust,
    "rust_toolchains",
    # musl rustc toolchains, re-registered in //bazel/toolchains with an
    # explicit @zig_sdk//libc:musl constraint: rules_rust's generated gnu and
    # musl toolchains share (os, cpu) constraints, so without the extra
    # constraint whichever registers first would win for both libcs.
    "rust_linux_aarch64__aarch64-unknown-linux-musl__nightly_tools",
    "rust_linux_aarch64__x86_64-unknown-linux-musl__nightly_tools",
    "rust_linux_x86_64__aarch64-unknown-linux-musl__nightly_tools",
    "rust_linux_x86_64__x86_64-unknown-linux-musl__nightly_tools",
    "rust_macos_aarch64__aarch64-unknown-linux-musl__nightly_tools",
    "rust_macos_aarch64__x86_64-unknown-linux-musl__nightly_tools",
)

# Order matters: repo-local toolchains (musl disambiguation wrappers, msvc
# cross cc toolchain) MUST resolve before the generated @rust_toolchains set.
register_toolchains("//bazel/toolchains:all")

register_toolchains("@rust_toolchains//:all")

# --- C/C++ toolchains ---------------------------------------------------------
# zig cc provides hermetic linux-gnu (pinned glibc 2.17 portability floor, same
# floor cargo-zigbuild used) and linux-musl cross toolchains, executable from
# both linux-x64 CI pods and darwin dev hosts. darwin targets use the hermetic
# clang + ld64.lld + Command Line Tools SDK toolchain in
# //bazel/toolchains/darwin from linux hosts and the host Xcode toolchain on mac
# hosts; win32-msvc uses the hermetic clang-cl+xwin toolchain in
# //bazel/toolchains/msvc.
zig = use_extension("@hermetic_cc_toolchain//toolchain:ext.bzl", "toolchains")
use_repo(zig, "zig_sdk")

register_toolchains(
    "@zig_sdk//libc_aware/toolchain:linux_amd64_gnu.2.17",
    "@zig_sdk//libc_aware/toolchain:linux_arm64_gnu.2.17",
    "@zig_sdk//libc_aware/toolchain:linux_amd64_musl",
    "@zig_sdk//libc_aware/toolchain:linux_arm64_musl",
)

# --- Host tools (crate_universe splicing / lockfile generation) ----------------
# Must be nightly: cargo's rustc target probe inherits user-level RUSTFLAGS
# (~/.cargo/config.toml commonly carries -Z flags on this repo's nightly
# toolchain), and a stable host rustc rejects them. Match rust.toolchain.
rust_host_tools = use_extension("@rules_rust//rust:extensions.bzl", "rust_host_tools")
rust_host_tools.host_tools(
    name = "rust_host_tools_nightly",
    version = "nightly/2026-11-08",
)
use_repo(rust_host_tools, "rust_host_tools_nightly")

# --- Third-party crates (crate_universe over the cargo workspace) --------------
crate = use_extension("@rules_rust//crate_universe:extensions.bzl", "crate")
crate.render_config(
    # rules_rust's builtin platform settings have no musl triples; ours in
    # //bazel/triples add the @zig_sdk//libc axis.
    platforms_template = "@@//bazel/triples:{triple}",
)
crate.from_cargo(
    name = "crates",
    cargo_lockfile = "//:Cargo.lock",
    # Nightly host tools (see the rust_host_tools extension above): the
    # splice's rustc probe must accept user-level -Z RUSTFLAGS.
    host_tools = "@rust_host_tools_nightly",
    # The root manifest covers all workspace members, including the vendored
    # crates (members so their sources render hermetically; the
    # [patch.crates-io] entries redirect registry deps to them).
    manifests = ["//:Cargo.toml"],
    # Exactly the shipped addon triples: crate BUILD files get
    # target_compatible_with selects over this set (defaults omit darwin-x64
    # and musl), and features/deps resolve per-triple from Cargo.lock.
    supported_platform_triples = [
        "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu",
        "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu",
        "x86_64-unknown-linux-musl",
        "aarch64-unknown-linux-musl",
        "x86_64-apple-darwin",
        "aarch64-apple-darwin",
        "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc",
        "aarch64-pc-windows-msvc",
    ],
)

# opusic-sys builds its bundled Opus via `cmake` and selects Ninja from PATH.
# The target-specific toolchain keeps MSVC cross builds on the wrapper
# compiler/linker; CFLAGS keeps Zig cross builds free of host UBSan links.
crate.annotation(
    build_script_env = {
        "CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE_x86_64_pc_windows_msvc": "$${pwd}/external/+msvc_cc_repository+msvc_cc/toolchain.cmake",
        "CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE_aarch64_pc_windows_msvc": "$${pwd}/external/+msvc_cc_repository+msvc_cc_arm64/toolchain.cmake",
        "CFLAGS": "-fno-sanitize=undefined",
        "PATH": "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/run/current-system/sw/bin",
    },
    crate = "opusic-sys",
    patch_args = ["-p1"],
    # CMake explicitly installs to lib; the upstream host-Linux lib64 search
    # points at a nonexistent directory even when cross-compiling for macOS.
    patches = ["//bazel/patches:opusic-sys-install-libdir.patch"],
    version = "0.7.5",
)

# wasmtime-c-api-impl (tree-sitter's `wasm` feature) runs `cmake -P` to install
# the C API headers tree-sitter compiles against; same host PATH as opusic-sys.
crate.annotation(
    build_script_env = {
        "PATH": "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/run/current-system/sw/bin",
    },
    crate = "wasmtime-c-api-impl",
)

# The bundled Wasmtime C API is static. wasm.h otherwise declares Windows
# imports, which is incompatible with the static archive tree-sitter links.
crate.annotation(
    build_script_env = {
        "CFLAGS_x86_64_pc_windows_msvc": "/DLIBWASM_STATIC",
        "CFLAGS_aarch64_pc_windows_msvc": "/DLIBWASM_STATIC",
    },
    crate = "tree-sitter",
)

# cargo-bazel omits workspace-local build dependencies from generated registry
# build scripts; restore nix 0.28's edge to the patched cfg_aliases crate.
crate.annotation(
    build_script_deps = ["@@//crates/vendor/cfg_aliases:cfg_aliases"],
    crate = "nix",
    version = "0.28.0",
)

# Same for normal dependencies: grep-printer's edge to the vendored
# grep-searcher (a workspace member via [patch.crates-io]) is dropped, so its
# rustc invocation has no `--extern grep_searcher`.
crate.annotation(
    crate = "grep-printer",
    deps = ["@@//crates/vendor/grep-searcher:grep-searcher"],
)

# Release addons must never pick up a host libpcre2 (Homebrew paths leaked into
# shipped dylibs before); always build the vendored static copy.
crate.annotation(
    build_script_env = {"PCRE2_SYS_STATIC": "1"},
    crate = "pcre2-sys",
)
use_repo(crate, "crates")

# --- msvc cross toolchain (owned by bazel/toolchains/msvc) ---------------------
# Hermetic clang-cl + lld-link + xwin CRT/SDK toolchain for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# (replaces cargo-xwin). Three repos so flag iteration in cc.bzl never
# invalidates the ~2 GiB LLVM download or the ~1 GiB xwin splat:
#   @llvm_msvc_tools  pruned LLVM 20.1.7 release binaries for the exec host
#                     (//bazel/toolchains:llvm.bzl)
#   @xwin_sysroot     MSVC CRT + Windows SDK splatted by pinned xwin 0.6.5
#   @msvc_cc          wrappers + MSVC-flavored cc_toolchain (rules_cc config)
# toolchain() registrations live in //bazel/toolchains (one per exec host).
# rules_cc pin matches Bazel 9.2's own builtin dependency.
bazel_dep(name = "rules_cc", version = "0.2.17")

llvm_msvc_tools = use_repo_rule("//bazel/toolchains:llvm.bzl", "llvm_msvc_tools_repository")

llvm_msvc_tools(name = "llvm_msvc_tools")

xwin_sysroot = use_repo_rule("//bazel/toolchains/msvc:sysroot.bzl", "xwin_sysroot_repository")

# Pinned like the arm64 splat below: the manifest's latest SDK (10.0.26100)
# no longer resolves x86_64 headers ("unable to find x86_64 headers").
xwin_sysroot(
    name = "xwin_sysroot",
    sdk_version = "10.0.22621",
)

xwin_sysroot(
    name = "xwin_sysroot_arm64",
    arch = "aarch64",
    sdk_version = "10.0.22621",
)

msvc_cc = use_repo_rule("//bazel/toolchains/msvc:cc.bzl", "msvc_cc_repository")

msvc_cc(name = "msvc_cc")

# aarch64-pc-windows-msvc variant (//:natives-win32-arm64).
msvc_cc(
    name = "msvc_cc_arm64",
    arch = "aarch64",
    xwin_repo = "@xwin_sysroot_arm64//:BUILD.bazel",
)

# blake3 assembles MASM .asm for x64 msvc targets; cc-rs resolves `ml64.exe`
# from the build-script PATH on non-windows hosts. Prepend @msvc_cc's wrapper
# dir (bin/ml64.exe → llvm-ml -m64; the dir rides into the sandbox with the
# resolved cc toolchain's all_files). ${pwd} expands to the exec root in the
# rules_rust build-script runner. The leading entry is the canonical repo path
# of @msvc_cc (`+<repo rule>+<name>`) — keep in sync if the rule or repo in
# this section is ever renamed. On non-msvc targets the dir simply does not
# exist and the rest of the PATH matches the opusic-sys annotation above.
crate.annotation(
    build_script_env = {
        "PATH": "$${pwd}/external/+msvc_cc_repository+msvc_cc/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin",
    },
    crate = "blake3",
)
# ring 0.17 compiles windows-aarch64 C/asm with GNU-driver `clang` from PATH
# (never clang-cl); @msvc_cc_arm64's bin/clang wrapper translates the toolchain
# CFLAGS and adds the xwin includes. Absent (and unused) for other targets.
crate.annotation(
    build_script_env = {
        "PATH": "$${pwd}/external/+msvc_cc_repository+msvc_cc_arm64/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin",
    },
    crate = "ring",
)
# psm (via wasmtime and stacker) assembles windows-aarch64 from its GAS source
# off a Windows host, but preprocesses that source only for GNU-style
# compilers; under clang-cl its GLOBL/FUNCTION macros stay unexpanded. Hand it
# @msvc_cc_arm64's GNU-driver clang (see the ring note). Absent elsewhere.
crate.annotation(
    build_script_env = {
        "CC_aarch64_pc_windows_msvc": "$${pwd}/external/+msvc_cc_repository+msvc_cc_arm64/bin/clang",
    },
    crate = "psm",
)
# --- end msvc cross toolchain ---------------------------------------------------

# --- darwin cross toolchain (owned by bazel/toolchains/darwin) -----------------
# Hermetic clang + ld64.lld cc toolchain for {arm64,x86_64}-apple-darwin from
# linux exec hosts, against the macOS SDK Apple ships in its Command Line Tools
# package. Mac hosts never fetch these (the toolchain()s are exec-gated on
# linux). Split like the msvc toolchain so flag iteration in cc.bzl never
# invalidates the downloads:
#   @llvm_darwin_tools      pruned LLVM 23.1.3 (clang, ld64.lld, llvm-ar, ...)
#   @macos_sdk              MacOSX27.0.sdk from Apple's software update CDN
#   @darwin_cc_{arm64,x64}  wrappers + macOS-flavored cc_toolchain
llvm_darwin_tools = use_repo_rule("//bazel/toolchains:llvm.bzl", "llvm_darwin_tools_repository")

llvm_darwin_tools(name = "llvm_darwin_tools")

macos_sdk = use_repo_rule("//bazel/toolchains/darwin:sdk.bzl", "macos_sdk_repository")

macos_sdk(name = "macos_sdk")

darwin_cc = use_repo_rule("//bazel/toolchains/darwin:cc.bzl", "darwin_cc_repository")

darwin_cc(
    name = "darwin_cc_arm64",
    arch = "arm64",
)

darwin_cc(
    name = "darwin_cc_x64",
    arch = "x86_64",
)

# Swift toolchains for the Apple Foundation Models bridge in pi-natives: the
# host probe for mac exec hosts, the pinned swift.org release for linux ones.
applefm_swift = use_repo_rule("//bazel/toolchains/swift:applefm.bzl", "applefm_swift_repository")

applefm_swift(name = "applefm_swift")

swift_linux = use_repo_rule("//bazel/toolchains/swift:linux.bzl", "swift_linux_repository")

swift_linux(name = "swift_linux")

# Cheap host-path overlay; unlike the pinned Swift download it must not be
# repo-content-cached because its symlinks point into other repositories.
swift_darwin_resources = use_repo_rule("//bazel/toolchains/swift:linux.bzl", "swift_darwin_resources_repository")

swift_darwin_resources(name = "swift_darwin_resources")
# --- end darwin cross toolchain -------------------------------------------------

> Fork permission policy: this build does not request `downloads`, `scripting`, or all-site host access and does not empty password-manager frames. Upstream 18.18.1 automatic frame recovery and 18.18.2 relay download tracking are omitted; Chrome may refuse a tab while another extension’s frame is present.

# @oh-my-pi/browser-relay

Chrome extension that lets omp's Eval `browser` API drive **your real Chrome tabs** — logged-in sessions included — without relaunching Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port` (which Chrome 136+ refuses on the default profile anyway). By default omp opens its own tab; `app.target` opts into an existing tab.

The companion relay server lives in the omp CLI (`omp browser-relay`, see `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/browser/relay/`). It impersonates Chrome's CDP discovery endpoint, synthesizes the browser target and `Target.*` hierarchy that `chrome.debugger` doesn't expose, and multiplexes any number of downstream puppeteer connections (omp opens one per tab worker) over the single debugger attachment Chrome allows per tab.

## Setup

1. `omp browser-relay install` — writes the bundled extension to `~/.omp/browser-relay/extension`, then load it via `chrome://extensions` → Developer mode → _Load unpacked_. (Or grab `omp-browser-relay-extension.zip` from GitHub releases.)
2. Opt in, one of two ways:
   - **Per call** — pass `app: "relay"` to `browser.open(...)` in Eval. Works without any setting and persists nothing: the configured default for every other call and session stays whatever it already was.
   - **As the default** — `omp config set browser.relay true` makes the relay the default for **every session using this profile, in every project** (project-level settings, `PI_BROWSER_RELAY`, and an explicit `app` choice still take precedence). Each session's `browser.open(...)` creates a separate background tab; an optional `url` navigates only that new tab, not the page you are reading.

That's it: the relay server auto-starts under omp's profile-independent global daemon broker the first time Eval's browser API needs it. Every relay consumer holds a broker lease, so one project exiting cannot interrupt another; the server stops after the last consumer across all projects exits. The extension badge turns **on** when connected. Run `omp browser-relay` manually only for `--token`, `--no-group`, or a non-default port — a relay already serving the port is adopted, never fought over.

Without `target`, omp creates a tab it owns and closes it when released. Creation and screenshots leave the foreground tab alone; an explicit `tab.bringToFront()` still activates the agent tab. `target` deliberately adopts a tab by URL/title substring instead; only one omp session can drive it at a time, and closing the session leaves that borrowed tab open.

Driven tabs join cyan `omp/<session ID>` groups within each Chrome window (the tab name is used when a caller has no session ID). The initial creation claim may briefly use the default `omp` group before the worker assigns the session group. Group labels are trimmed to 32 characters; groups dissolve on disconnect, and debugger attachments/infobars are released when no session holds the tab. Other tabs, pinned tabs, tabs in unrelated user groups, and tabs deliberately dragged out are left alone. The `omp` and `omp/*` group titles are reserved for the relay and are dissolved on disconnect. Disable grouping with `omp browser-relay --no-group`.

After an omp upgrade, the relay keeps the extension current on its own: when it meets an extension older than itself that Chrome loaded from `~/.omp/browser-relay/extension`, and no omp session is connected to the relay and none of the extension's tabs is attached, it rewrites the files there and asks the extension to reload. Chrome re-reads them under the same extension id, keeping its settings, permissions and the _Allow access to file URLs_ choice; the badge goes off and on. Otherwise run `omp browser-relay install` (with your `--dir`) and click _Reload_ in `chrome://extensions`: after every upgrade for an extension loaded from another folder, once for one installed before omp could update it. A Chrome restart is not enough, as Chrome keeps running the worker it loaded; a relay `browser.open` notes when the loaded extension came from an older omp.

## Development

- `bun run build` — bundles the extension into `dist/extension/`, zips it for GH releases, and regenerates the embedded CLI install assets under `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/browser/relay/extension-assets/` (**commit those**).
- `bun scripts/smoke.ts [relay-url] [target-substring]` — end-to-end smoke replicating omp's supervisor + tab-worker double-connection pattern against a live relay.

## Limitations

- `chrome://`, DevTools, Web Store, and other-extension pages are not attachable and are hidden from the agent.
- Chrome shows its "is debugging this browser" infobar while any tab is attached; dismissing it detaches that tab until it navigates again.
- A tab with DevTools open can't be attached (one debugger per tab — the constraint the relay multiplexes around for its own clients).
- Chrome refuses the debugger in a tab while another extension's frame, such as a password manager's inline menu, is in it. This fork leaves those frames untouched and reports Chrome's refusal. Close the other extension's popup yourself before retrying.
- Anything that can reach the relay port can drive your logged-in browser. The relay binds loopback only; use `omp browser-relay --token <secret>` (mirrored in the extension options) if untrusted local processes are a concern.

Relay tabs do not support download tracking or download-path lookup in this fork. Explicitly select a non-relay browser to use the existing download helpers; relay calls do not request broader extension permissions.
